truth_states: FACT = source-derived; UPSTREAM = in-tree doc claim; INFERENCE = labeled reasoning; AUTHORITY = HX governance decision

entries.name: healthz-lifecycle-phase-probe
entries.purpose: Unauthenticated GET/HEAD /healthz maps the process lifecycle phase (starting/ready/stopping) to 200 'ok' only when ready, else 503 with the phase name as the plain-text body — the orchestrator-grade readiness signal. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only phase report; wrong phase reporting only misleads orchestrators, no data path
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET /healthz during boot (expect 503 'starting'), after ready (200 'ok'), during shutdown (503 'stopping'); HEAD variant returns status with null body
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/healthz/route.ts; path falls through to the /api catch-all (not applicable to /healthz top-level — verify 404)

entries.name: healthz-event-loop-lag-watchdog
entries.purpose: Every GET /healthz observes mean event-loop lag via node:perf_hooks monitorEventLoopDelay and logs a throttled [HEALTHZ] warning (10s suppression) when lag exceeds 200ms, on the premise that a 200 from a busy loop is not healthy (#10303). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — warn-only telemetry; never changes the response
entries.test_contract: Direct: block the event loop >200ms, GET /healthz, assert the throttled warning line; negative: second request within 10s does not re-warn
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the observeHealthzEventLoopLag() call at src/app/healthz/route.ts:27 — warn-only, no behavioral dependency

entries.name: public-liveness-api-health
entries.purpose: GET /api/health is the canonical unauthenticated liveness probe returning only {status:'ok', timestamp} with no-store headers; the doc comment states version/uptime/memory are deliberately withheld from this public surface and reserved for authenticated /api/monitoring/health. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — public unauthenticated endpoint; any future field added here is instantly public on an exposed instance
entries.test_contract: Direct: unauthenticated GET returns 200 {status,timestamp}; negative: response carries no version/memory/uptime keys
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/health/route.ts; /api/health falls to the #6424 JSON catch-all

entries.name: public-db-ping-probe
entries.purpose: GET /api/health/ping is an unauthenticated probe that calls pingDb() and returns {status,timestamp,latencyMs} at 200, or 503 {status:'error', error:'db_query_failed'} when the database does not answer — built for high-frequency polling where /api/monitoring/health is too expensive. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — public endpoint whose 503 reveals DB-health transitions (timing signal), deliberately accepted for probe use
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET returns 200 with latencyMs under normal DB; negative/fault: with DB broken returns 503 db_query_failed
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/health/ping/route.ts; path falls to JSON catch-all 404

entries.name: monitoring-health-aggregated-observability-snapshot
entries.purpose: GET /api/monitoring/health aggregates 8+ subsystems (circuit breakers, rate-limit status + learned limits, model lockouts, quota monitor, active sessions, credential health, local providers, adaptive + structural chat admission, dedup inflight) into one payload with a 1s TTL cache; anonymous callers receive only {status, setupComplete} (GHSA-mvf8-qc78-5mxm host-fingerprinting fix — full view requires management auth); DELETE resets all circuit breakers (auth required) and invalidates the cache. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the payload fingerprints host/version/pid/memory/provider config; the anonymous-vs-full split at line 37 is the control that keeps it safe, and DELETE mutates breaker state
entries.test_contract: Direct (anonymous): GET returns only status/setupComplete; direct (management token): full payload with all subsystem keys; mutation: DELETE with auth resets breakers and reports resetCount; negative: unauthenticated DELETE is 401
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/monitoring/health/route.ts — monitoring degrades to the per-subsystem endpoints; breaker reset reverts to per-module APIs

entries.name: graceful-degradation-registry-and-report
entries.purpose: A domain registry tracks per-feature degradation levels (full/reduced/minimal/default) for services with external dependencies; GET /api/health/degradation exposes the report (or a summary view) so the dashboard can show which features are running degraded and why. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only status registry; misreported degradation hides operator signal but mutates nothing
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET returns active flag + per-feature report; seeded fault: degrade one registered feature and confirm it appears with its level and reason
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/health/degradation/route.ts; registry keeps working internally, only the HTTP view disappears

entries.name: db-health-diagnosis-and-autorepair
entries.purpose: GET /api/db/health (authenticated) runs runManagedDbHealthCheck({autoRepair:false}) reporting integrity/reference/stale-snapshot/invalid-state issues plus driver durability (sql.js WASM or :memory: flagged degraded); POST runs the same check with autoRepair:true, repairing issues and reporting repairedCount/backupCreated. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — POST mutates the primary SQLite store (repair path); GET is read-only; both are management-authenticated
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET returns isHealthy + issues[] + driver block; mutation: POST on a seeded broken reference returns repairedCount>0 and backupCreated; negative: unauthenticated GET/POST return 401
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the route file; manual sqlite3 integrity_check remains as the offline fallback

entries.name: subsystem-health-endpoints
entries.purpose: Specialized health routes: /api/memory/health (management-auth, verifies the memory extraction pipeline), /api/storage/health (DB driver/path/size/last-backup/retention from the DATA_DIR), and /api/token-health (aggregate OAuth-token health counts healthy/errored/lastCheck across active oauth connections). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only subsystem probes; memory/health is management-gated, storage and token-health expose only operational metadata
entries.test_contract: Direct: each endpoint returns its documented shape; negative (memory): unauthenticated returns the management-auth rejection
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the individual route.ts files; each subsystem keeps functioning without its probe

entries.name: local-provider-health-poller
entries.purpose: Background poller for localhost provider_nodes: GET /models with a 5s timeout, exponential backoff 30s→60s→120s→300s on consecutive failures resetting to 30s on first success, 15s initial boot delay, health kept in-memory (no DB migration), Promise.allSettled so one slow node never blocks the sweep. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — outbound loopback probes only; a false 'down' marking shifts routing away from a healthy local node (availability, not integrity)
entries.test_contract: Direct: stand up a stub /models endpoint, watch it marked healthy; negative: kill it and observe backoff schedule and isHealthy=false; persistence: state is process-memory only (restart resets)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Env/code path: poller never starts when disabled by test/build guards; remove start call to disable permanently

entries.name: provider-health-matrix
entries.purpose: GET /api/providers/health-matrix (management-auth) builds a per-account, per-model health matrix over 1h/24h/7d/30d windows — success rate, latency, lockout state/reason/remaining, cooldown/backoff, rate-limited-until — joining usage history, circuit breakers, model lockouts and web-session pool health. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only aggregation; management-gated so the per-account detail stays internal
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET with range=24h returns account/model rows with the documented fields; negative: unauthenticated request rejected; boundary: range outside the enum rejected by zod
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the route + card; no runtime dependency (dashboard read path only)

entries.name: health-autopilot-remediation-actions
entries.purpose: Provider and combo health autopilots analyze breaker/cooldown/lockout/error state and propose typed remediation actions (clear_provider_breaker, clear_connection_cooldown, clear_stale_connection_error, clear_model_lockout, reactivate/deactivate_connection) with risk labels, confirmation flags and precondition hashes; combo autopilot joins provider report + combo health + forecast. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the actions mutate routing-affecting state (breakers, lockouts, connection activation) when executed; proposals themselves are read-only, precondition hash guards stale approvals
entries.test_contract: Direct: seed a locked-out model and confirm the report proposes clear_model_lockout with a preconditionsHash; negative: executing with a stale hash is rejected; mutation: execute reactivate_connection and verify the connection row flips active
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not wire the execute endpoints (dashboard-only proposals); disabling autopilot removes proposals without changing underlying state

entries.name: credential-health-cache-and-token-health-sweep
entries.purpose: An in-memory per-connection credential-health cache (status/lastError/consecutiveFailures/responseTime with TTL auto-expiry) feeds the monitoring payload, while the JobRegistry-run token_health_check job sweeps OAuth tokens every 60s (honoring OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_TOKEN_HEALTHCHECK, build phase, and test-process guards). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — cache is read-through telemetry; the sweep touches live OAuth refresh paths so a bug there degrades credential freshness signal
entries.test_contract: Direct: cache read returns fresh entry; TTL expiry returns stale/miss; job: run handler once and assert recordsAffected==swept count; disable: OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_TOKEN_HEALTHCHECK set → handler no-ops with success
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_DISABLE_TOKEN_HEALTHCHECK=true (documented kill switch); unregister the job from the registry

entries.name: embedded-services-health-checker
entries.purpose: HealthChecker class polls embedded services' health URLs on an interval with a 5s fetch timeout, flips state to down after 3 consecutive failures, notifies via onChange callback, and unrefs its timer so the poller never keeps the process alive. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — loopback/embedded-service probes; wrong state only affects service-status display and restart decisions
entries.test_contract: Direct: point at a stub health URL, observe healthy transition; negative: 3 failed polls → down state via onChange; lifecycle: stop() resets to unknown
entries.rollback_or_disable: Do not instantiate HealthChecker for a service; no persistent state to roll back

entries.name: request-phase-telemetry-aggregator
entries.purpose: RequestTelemetry times 7 named request phases (parse, validate, policy, resolve, connect, stream, finalize) per request; a process-local aggregator keeps the last 1000 completed summaries (MAX_HISTORY, FIFO shift) and computes count/avg/p50/p95/p99 plus per-phase breakdowns over a sliding window (default 5min). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — in-memory timing telemetry; loss on restart only erases percentile history
entries.test_contract: Direct: drive N requests, call getTelemetrySummary and verify count/percentile math on known durations; boundary: >1000 records evicts oldest
entries.rollback_or_disable: Stop calling recordTelemetry at the instrumentation points; aggregator idles empty (no flag exists — code-level disable)

entries.name: telemetry-summary-endpoint
entries.purpose: GET /api/telemetry/summary returns the request-telemetry window summary (windowMs query param, default 300000) joined with quota-monitor summary, active sessions, process uptime, memoryUsage, activeConnections and a derived errorRate. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — exposes process memoryUsage and uptime; on an anonymous-keyless deployment this leaks host operational detail (no publicView filtering seen here, unlike /api/monitoring/health) [INFERENCE: auth classification depends on the central P4 pipeline, not this file]
entries.test_contract: Direct: GET ?windowMs=60000 returns count/percentiles plus uptime/memoryUsage keys; cross-check activeConnections equals session manager count
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove src/app/api/telemetry/summary/route.ts; telemetry aggregation remains in-process

entries.name: otlp-genai-routing-event-sink
entries.purpose: Optional lightweight OpenTelemetry sink: when OMNIROUTE_OTEL_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set, routing events are forwarded as GenAI semantic-convention spans to a collector's OTLP/HTTP JSON /v1/traces endpoint via global fetch (no @opentelemetry SDK), buffered O(1) with oldest-dropped overflow (never backpressuring the data plane), batch default 64, service name 'omniroute'; explicitly documents that no secrets/prompts are serialized. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — egress of routing metadata (provider/model/token-usage attributes) to an operator-chosen collector; disabled by default so the shipped posture sends nothing
entries.test_contract: Direct: set OMNIROUTE_OTEL_ENDPOINT to a capture stub, issue routed requests, assert GenAI-semconv spans arrive; negative: with env unset isRoutingOtelEnabled() is false and zero OTel code runs; overload: flood events and confirm oldest-dropped, never request-path blocking
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unset OMNIROUTE_OTEL_ENDPOINT / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT — documented as fully inert when unconfigured

entries.name: combo-metrics-inmemory-tracker
entries.purpose: In-memory per-combo metrics: total/success/failure/fallback counts, latency sums, strategy, intent counts, and per-model/per-target breakdowns (executionKey/stepId/provider/connection) readable via getComboMetrics for the dashboard. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — process-local counters; restart resets history (dashboard reads go empty, no correctness impact)
entries.test_contract: Direct: run combo traffic, call getComboMetrics(comboName) and verify counts/latency averages; persistence: restart and confirm counters reset (documented in-memory design)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove recording calls at dispatch sites; getComboMetrics returns null (no flag — code-level)

entries.name: combo-health-aggregation-service
entries.purpose: buildComboHealthResponse joins combo records, usage-history performance rows (requests/success/latency per model), quota snapshots (remaining %/exhaustion), and in-memory combo metrics into the combo-health dashboard view consumed by /api/usage/combo-health* endpoints. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only aggregation over existing stores
entries.test_contract: Direct: seed usage rows + quota snapshot, verify the response carries per-model performance and quota fields; cross-check the /api/usage/combo-health endpoint serves this builder's output
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the endpoint wiring; underlying data sources unaffected

entries.name: pino-structured-logger-with-redaction-hook
entries.purpose: Primary logger is pino with ISO timestamps, base {service:'omniroute'}, level from APP_LOG_LEVEL (debug in dev, info in prod), a hooks.logMethod wrapper that runs every log call through redactLogArgs before emission, and a multi-target transport (stdout + optional file) whose error listener drops failed writes instead of crashing the process (#6360). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the redaction hook is the last defense against credential leakage into logs; a regression here leaks secrets to disk/stdout
entries.test_contract: Direct: log a string containing 'Bearer abcdef...' and assert [REDACTED] in output; fault: delete the log directory mid-run and confirm the process survives with a stderr notice
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set APP_LOG_TO_FILE=false to drop the file target; removing the hook reverts to raw pino (never recommended)

entries.name: log-secret-redaction-net
entries.purpose: Bounded-regex redaction library: a cheap SECRET_HINT pre-test skips clean strings, then five bounded patterns scrub Authorization/Bearer values, x-api-key/api_key values, Telegram bot tokens, and sk-* style keys to [REDACTED]; recursive object/error redaction is depth-6 / 2000-node capped with a circular guard — explicitly a complement to call-site maskers, not a replacement. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — this is the safety net for every log line in the process; pattern regressions or ReDoS-prone edits either leak credentials or hang the logger
entries.test_contract: Direct: unit-feed each secret shape and assert redaction; negative: a 1MB clean string passes through unchanged (hint pre-test); adversarial: pathological input completes within the bounded patterns
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the hook wiring in logger.ts (reverts to unredacted logging — disable only the file, never the discipline)

entries.name: app-log-file-rotation-retention
entries.purpose: File logging defaults ON (APP_LOG_TO_FILE!=='false') to DATA_DIR/logs/application/app.log, rotated at 50MB (APP_LOG_MAX_FILE_SIZE), retaining 7 days (APP_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS) and at most 20 rotated files (APP_LOG_MAX_FILES), with a 60s runtime rotation-check interval; the default path is DATA_DIR-anchored so a globally-installed CLI never silently no-ops (#6197). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — log files on disk accumulate request metadata; rotation caps bound disk growth, and a misconfigured path writes outside the data dir
entries.test_contract: Direct: write past 50MB and observe rotation; retention: age files beyond 7 days and confirm cleanup; count: >20 rotated files pruned to 20
entries.rollback_or_disable: APP_LOG_TO_FILE=false (documented env kill switch)

entries.name: open-sse-tag-console-logger
entries.purpose: The traffic-plane (open-sse) logger: tag-based or request-scoped console logging with levels debug/info/warn/error gated by APP_LOG_LEVEL (default info) and APP_LOG_FORMAT switching text '[LEVEL] [TAG] msg {meta}' vs single-line JSON, plus generateRequestId (req_<ts>_<counter>) for correlation. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — console-only output on the hot path; format/level misconfiguration affects log volume, not traffic
entries.test_contract: Direct: APP_LOG_FORMAT=json emits parseable single-line JSON; level gate: APP_LOG_LEVEL=warn suppresses info lines
entries.rollback_or_disable: Code-level only (no disable flag); reverting the module restores console.* defaults

entries.name: legacy-structured-json-file-logger
entries.purpose: A second structured logger (debug10/info20/warn30/error40/fatal50) emits human-readable dev output or production JSON and independently appends JSON lines to the app log file when APP_LOG_TO_FILE is enabled, pulling correlation IDs from middleware — parallel to the pino stack. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — duplicate write path to the same app log (both this and pino append); its best-effort writeToFile swallows errors by design
entries.test_contract: Direct: emit at each level and verify JSON-lines appended to APP_LOG_FILE_PATH; fault: unwritable path → app continues (silent catch)
entries.rollback_or_disable: APP_LOG_TO_FILE=false stops its file appends too; module removal reverts call sites to pino

entries.name: per-key-no-log-compliance-filter
entries.purpose: Compliance no-log set: API key IDs from NO_LOG_API_KEY_IDS plus runtime setNoLog() calls (mirrored to an api_keys.no_log DB column when present, PRAGMA-verified once, 30s cache) are excluded from call logging — the mechanism for honoring per-key privacy requirements. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — a regression here silently logs traffic the operator marked do-not-log (compliance breach); DB-column probe failure degrades to env-only set
entries.test_contract: Direct: setNoLog(id,true) then drive traffic with that key and assert no call_log rows; persistence: restart with only env var set and confirm env-seeded keys still suppressed
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the key from NO_LOG_API_KEY_IDS / setNoLog(id,false) — logging resumes

entries.name: proxy-hybrid-ringbuffer-sqlite-logger
entries.purpose: Proxy/event logger keeps a 200-entry in-memory ring buffer for real-time dashboard reads and persists the same entries to the SQLite proxy_logs table (skipped in cloud/build phases), capturing status, proxy level, provider, targetUrl, inbound clientIp AND outbound egressIp (the account's exit IP), latency, error, connection/combo/account, and TLS-fingerprint flag. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — persisted rows carry client and egress IPs plus target URLs (privacy surface); bounded by table max-rows retention settings
entries.test_contract: Direct: emit entries and verify both ring read and DB rows; persistence: restart and confirm hydration from DB; retention: table capped at PROXY_LOGS_TABLE_MAX_ROWS (default 100000, logEnv.ts:11)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Purge via /api/settings/purge-proxy-logs family; persistence is skipped automatically in cloud/build phases

entries.name: call-log-payload-sensitive-key-masking
entries.purpose: Call-log payload writer masks a fixed SENSITIVE_KEYS set (api_key/apiKey, authorization, x-api-key, x-goog-api-key, access/refresh tokens, password, secret, token, cookie, storageState, runtimeKey) and runs bodies through sanitizePII before persisting — deliberately scoped to true credential field names so diagnostic fields like 'capabilities' survive. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — call-log artifacts on disk would otherwise hold provider credentials and session cookies (web-impersonation providers surface secrets in bodies, per the in-source comment)
entries.test_contract: Direct: write a payload containing each sensitive key and assert masked artifact; negative: a body with 'capabilities' survives unmasked (documented non-goal)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Code-level only; removing the masker reverts to raw artifact writes (never recommended)

entries.name: client-apikey-redis-fixed-window-rate-limit
entries.purpose: Client-facing per-API-key request rate limiting: validateRateLimitAndThrottle builds rules (per-key custom rateLimits, else DEFAULT+ENV defaults plus maxRequestsPerDay/Minute) and enforces them via an atomic Redis Lua multi-rule fixed-window script (window keys with 2x TTL), falling back to a process-local in-memory store with bounded O(n) stale-window eviction when REDIS_URL is unset, failing OPEN on Redis eval errors, then applying an optional per-key throttleDelayMs (capped 300s). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — the only request-rate control on the client traffic plane; fail-open on Redis outage means limit bypass during cache failure, and in-memory fallback is per-process (limits multiply across replicas)
dependencies: Redis via ioredis when REDIS_URL set (lazy import, key prefix 'omniroute:')
entries.test_contract: Direct: configure limit=2/60s on a key, 3rd request in-window gets 429 'Request limit exceeded (60s window)'; fallback: unset REDIS_URL and repeat against the in-memory store; fault: kill Redis mid-test → requests pass (documented fail-open); negative: throttleDelayMs adds measurable delay
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove a key's rateLimits and defaults to disable per-key limiting; the check no-ops when no rules exist (rateLimiter.ts:230)

entries.name: api-key-token-limit-policy
entries.purpose: Per-key token budgets enforced in the policy chain: validateTokenLimit calls checkTokenLimits(apiKeyId, provider, model) and rejects breaches with 429 naming scope and used/limit tokens; recordTokenUsage increments billable-token windows post-request (provider/model-scoped counters with reset-log rows on window rollover). [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — token overspend control per key; check failure is fail-closed (503 'Token limit policy unavailable') unlike the rate limiter
entries.test_contract: Direct: set a small per-model token limit and drive requests until 429 with 'Token limit exceeded for model ...'; negative: counter increments only for billable tokens (record path no-ops on <=0)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Clear the key's token-limit configuration; validateTokenLimit returns null when no breach/limit

entries.name: api-key-daily-weekly-usd-usage-limits
entries.purpose: Optional per-key cost ceilings (usageLimitEnabled with dailyUsageLimitUsd/weeklyUsageLimitUsd): status computed from spend rows with daily/weekly window boundaries (Fortaleza UTC-3 anchored), exposing dailySpentUsd/weeklySpentUsd and exceeded flags via the management endpoint GET /api/keys/[id]/usage-limits. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — spend-capping control per client key; enforcement correctness depends on cost-calculator fidelity (cross-ref P3 usage accounting)
dependencies: quota reset events for window starts
entries.test_contract: Direct: enable a $0.01 daily limit, drive billable traffic, assert dailyExceeded flips and the API reports it; boundary: window rolls at the documented UTC-3 midnight anchor
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set usageLimitEnabled=false on the key (status endpoint reports enabled:false)

entries.name: provider-adaptive-bottleneck-rate-limit-manager
entries.purpose: Upstream-side adaptive limiting: per provider+connection Bottleneck limiters auto-learn limits from response headers (x-ratelimit-*, retry-after, anthropic-ratelimit-*), enabled by default for API-key providers and disabled for OAuth, togglable per connection; learned limits (max 200 entries) persist debounced every 60s, with a wedge watchdog replacing stuck limiters. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — mislearned reservoirs throttle or burst against upstream quotas; per-process state means each replica learns independently
entries.test_contract: Direct: drive responses carrying x-ratelimit-remaining/reset and verify the limiter reservoir updates (getLearnedLimits); negative: OAuth connection has no limiter by default; persistence: learned limits survive debounced save/restore
entries.rollback_or_disable: Per-connection dashboard toggle (disableRateLimitProtection); global: no kill switch — per-connection only

entries.name: provider-rate-limit-state-db-persistence
entries.purpose: Rate-limited-until state is persisted directly on provider_connections.rate_limited_until so cooldowns survive OAuth token refreshes (which must not clear the field) — sub2api-derived fix preventing premature retry of rate-limited accounts. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — a stuck timestamp keeps an account parked (availability); OAuth flows are the corruption vector the design guards
entries.test_contract: Persistence: set a connection rate-limited, run the token-refresh path, assert rate_limited_until survives; negative: clearing sets NULL and re-enables the account
entries.rollback_or_disable: setConnectionRateLimitUntil(id, null) clears the cooldown

entries.name: provider-default-sliding-window-fallback
entries.purpose: For providers that send no rate-limit headers (so the adaptive path learns nothing), a static sliding-window limiter enforces documented caps — currently only nvidia (40 req/60s plus a per-connection concurrency cap of 6) — with operator overrides resolved from resilience settings; no-op for every other provider. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — proactive throttling only; a wrong static entry under-throttles (upstream 429s) or over-throttles (lost throughput) one provider
entries.test_contract: Direct: send 41 nvidia requests in 60s and observe the 41st delayed/queued by the window; negative: another provider sees zero behavior change (documented no-op)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the PROVIDER_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS entry / override to null — path becomes a no-op

entries.name: per-model-concurrency-semaphore
entries.purpose: Per-model FIFO concurrency gate for the round-robin combo strategy: at max concurrency requests queue instead of failing, rate-limited models pause their queue, and an optional maxQueueSize rejects over-deep waits with SEMAPHORE_QUEUE_FULL so the combo loop cascades immediately; all state is in-memory by design. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — unbounded historical queue behavior can park requests under a wedged upstream; bounded queue option changes failover latency characteristics
entries.test_contract: Direct: hold maxConcurrency requests, issue one more and verify FIFO acquisition on release; negative: maxQueueSize=0 rejects immediately with SEMAPHORE_QUEUE_FULL; timeout: queued acquire rejects after timeoutMs
entries.rollback_or_disable: Omit maxQueueSize to restore historical unbounded queue; state resets on restart (documented)

entries.name: upstream-waf-burst-guard
entries.purpose: agentrouter.org WAF guard: serializes outbound calls per provider with a minimum 500ms inter-request gap so request bursts do not trip the upstream content-filter WAF into 400 content-blocked responses; in-memory per-provider last-sent state, conservative default tuned below human latency perception. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — added latency floor (500ms) on one provider path; per-process state means replicas can still jointly burst
entries.test_contract: Direct: fire two rapid agentrouter calls and measure >=500ms spacing; negative: non-agentrouter providers are unaffected
entries.rollback_or_disable: configureWafRateLimit({minGapMs:0}) or remove the guard call from the executor

entries.name: gemini-rpd-rpm-tpm-classifier-tracker
entries.purpose: In-memory Gemini counters (daily RPD, sliding-60s RPM, sliding-60s TPM) fed by published per-model limits from geminiRateLimits.json, used to classify Gemini's identical 429 bodies as quota_exhausted vs rate_limit_exceeded vs token_rate_exceeded. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — classification only (error semantics/failover messaging); counters are per-process and reset daily by date key
entries.test_contract: Direct: drive a model to its published RPD in the tracker, force a 429, assert classification quota_exhausted; negative: a fresh date key resets daily counts
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the instrumentation calls; classification falls back to generic 429 handling

entries.name: chat-body-admission-heavyweight-gate
entries.purpose: Process-local admission gate for POST /v1/chat/completions: ONE global heavyweight budget shared by all keys/sessions (fake-credential-sharding resistant), reserving capacity before parsing and enforcing against bytes actually read (not Content-Length); heavyweight threshold 256KB (OMNIROUTE_CHAT_LARGE_BODY_BYTES), hard body cap 50MB, max 1 heavy in flight by default, bounded 2s queue wait (retryable 503 instead of instant rejection for agent fan-out), and a 4MB queued-bytes budget charging parked waiters' buffered bodies. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — this is the heap-exhaustion defense on the hottest path (#4380 class); misconfiguration either OOMs the process or serializes all chat traffic to concurrency 1
entries.test_contract: Direct: two >256KB concurrent bodies → second waits then 200; load: exceed queue budget → retryable 503; negative: small bodies bypass the heavyweight path; boundary: >50MB body rejected pre-parse
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_CHAT_MAX_HEAVY_IN_FLIGHT / OMNIROUTE_CHAT_ADMISSION_QUEUE_MS=0 restores legacy immediate-reject behavior; no full off switch (structural)

entries.name: ingest-byte-budget-autocalibration
entries.purpose: Auto-derived process-wide ingest byte budget: min(V8 heap limit, cgroup constrainedMemory) × 0.25 heap fraction ÷ 8 amplification, clamped to [8MB, 2GB], with OMNIROUTE_CHAT_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES override — so the admission gate scales from a 512MB container to a 32GB host without env tuning, cached after first resolution. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the budget value IS the admission ceiling; a wrong cgroup read under-reserves (OOM risk) or over-reserves (needless 503s)
entries.test_contract: Direct: on a constrained container verify budget == clamp(cgroup*0.25/8); override: OMNIROUTE_CHAT_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES=16MB yields source 'override'; boundary: sub-128MiB host hits the 8MB floor
entries.rollback_or_disable: OMNIROUTE_CHAT_MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES override pins the budget manually (documented escape hatch)

entries.name: adaptive-admission-controller-shadow-mode
entries.purpose: Adaptive admission layer: a cost-based concurrency controller (min 8 / initial 64 / max 1000, queue caps 128 count / 2000 cost, 5s max wait, 1s window) that ships in 'shadow' mode by default — it computes would-admit/would-queue/would-reject decisions for the health payload without enforcing, configurable via ADAPTIVE_ADMISSION_* env keys, integrated with resource-pressure signals. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — enforcing mode changes production admission behavior globally; shadow mode is telemetry-only and safe
entries.test_contract: Direct: read the snapshot in /api/monitoring/health and confirm mode 'shadow' with wouldAdmit counters moving under load; mutation: ADAPTIVE_ADMISSION_MODE=enforce turns decisions live (requires owner sign-off per HX governance)
entries.rollback_or_disable: ADAPTIVE_ADMISSION_MODE=shadow (the shipped default) or leave the env unset

entries.name: session-fingerprint-sticky-manager
entries.purpose: Session fingerprinting for sticky routing and prompt-cache affinity: stable session IDs hashed from model/provider/system-prompt/first-message/tools signature, tracked in an in-memory map hard-capped at 200 sessions with 15-minute TTL eviction every 60s (oldest evicted over cap), plus per-API-key active-session sets for the dashboard. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — sticky-routing state lives here; cap eviction silently re-homes long sessions to other accounts (cache-locality loss), and fingerprints derived from prompt content are a correlation surface
dependencies: request bodies (system prompt, first user message, tools)
entries.test_contract: Direct: same conversation shape twice → identical session ID; boundary: create 201 sessions and verify oldest eviction below the 200 cap; TTL: idle 15min + sweep → session gone
entries.rollback_or_disable: Code-level only; removing generateSessionId calls reverts to non-sticky routing

entries.name: exclusive-connection-session-leases
entries.purpose: Client-facing lease protocol (POST /api/v1/session-leases, API-key authed): zod-discriminated acquire/renew/release actions with positive-safe generation counters and typed release reasons (OWNER_EXIT, CLIENT_CANCELLED) over exclusive provider connections; occupancy authority is the SQLite exclusive_connection_leases table, projected into the dashboard /api/sessions view alongside in-memory sessions. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — leases serialize exclusive account access; generation-counter or release bugs either double-book a connection (upstream account conflict) or wedge it leased forever
entries.test_contract: Direct: acquire returns state+generation+expiry; fencing: renew with a stale generation rejected; lifecycle: release with OWNER_EXIT frees occupancy visible in /api/sessions; negative: unauthenticated POST is 401 LEASE_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the lease rows server-side to force-release; clients without lease support are unaffected (opt-in protocol)

entries.name: quota-share-engine-enforcement
entries.purpose: Quota Sharing Engine hot-path gate: enforceQuotaShare (PRE-request; wired into chatCore and embeddings handlers) resolves the key's pool allocation and plan dimensions, applies per-(key,model) caps (hourly window, 429 'model-cap' with quota.exceeded webhook), fair-share decisions with a 0.5 saturation threshold, and blocks with sanitized 429s; recordConsumption tracks post-response usage fire-and-forget; the whole engine is FAIL-OPEN by design (B16) so quota-infrastructure errors never block traffic. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — fail-open means quota infra failure silently lifts all sharing limits; conversely a saturation-signal bug blocks paying traffic with 429s
entries.test_contract: Direct: allocate a key with a tiny pool cap and drive to 429; negative: break the store (DB down) and confirm requests still pass (B16); model-cap: cap one model, verify sibling models in the same pool unaffected
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the key's pool allocations (engine returns allow when no pool matches); no global kill switch beyond empty allocations

entries.name: quota-store-sliding-window-sqlite-redis
entries.purpose: Quota consumption storage: sliding-window counter with 2 buckets per (apiKey, dimension) (effective = prev×(1−elapsed/window)+curr), per-key in-memory mutex serializing read-modify-write, SQLite default driver selectable to Redis via DB setting quotaStore.driver or QUOTA_STORE_DRIVER env (Redis URL via setting/env, invalid → sqlite fallback with warning, never throws); driver change via settings API resets the singleton. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — SQLite driver is single-process (sharing limits don't span replicas); the sliding window approximates rates (bounded drift vs fixed windows)
entries.test_contract: Direct: consume cost across a window boundary and verify the weighted-effective math; concurrency: parallel consumes serialize via mutex without lost updates; driver: set redis driver with bad URL → falls back to sqlite and logs
entries.rollback_or_disable: PUT /api/settings/quota-store driver=sqlite (default); singleton reset picks it up on next call

entries.name: quota-pools-and-allocations-crud
entries.purpose: Persistence for quota_pools and quota_allocations: pools group provider connections with per-API-key weight+cap+policy allocations; every mutation is prepared-statement SQL, and pool changes fire serialized background maintenance that auto-mints/prunes the matching quotaShared-* combos without ever breaking pool CRUD on combo failure. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — allocation rows define who gets what share; the auto-combo hook silently changes routing-visible combos on pool edits (operational surprise vector)
entries.test_contract: Direct: create pool + allocation, verify rows and the auto-minted quotaShared-* combo; negative: combo-maintenance failure leaves pool CRUD successful (documented fire-and-forget); cleanup: pool deletion prunes its combos
entries.rollback_or_disable: DELETE the pool (guarded cleanup removes minted combos); allocations can be zeroed without deleting the pool

entries.name: active-session-quota-monitor
entries.purpose: Per-connection active quota polling (opt-in via providerSpecificData.quotaMonitorEnabled, default false): adaptive interval 60s normal → 15s critical (≥80% warn, ≥95% exhausted), session-deduplicated alerts within a 5-minute suppression window, unref'd timers, and snapshots feeding the monitoring health payload. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — outbound quota-API polling; wrong exhaustion classification parks accounts early (availability) but never blocks the request path directly
entries.test_contract: Direct: enable on a connection with a stub fetcher reporting 96% → status exhausted, 15s polling; alert: second alert within 5min suppressed; disable: flag off → monitor idles
entries.rollback_or_disable: providerSpecificData.quotaMonitorEnabled=false (the shipped default)

entries.name: internal-budget-guard-evaluator
entries.purpose: Pure budget evaluator for internal limits: scoped (global/provider/model/pool), period (daily/weekly/monthly), typed (currency/tokens/requests) limits with a warning threshold returning allow/warn/deny — deny on exhaustion, deny on invalid config (non-finite usage or non-positive limit), warn past the threshold fraction. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — deny decisions block traffic; invalid-config fail-closed (deny) is the safe direction but can wedge a misconfigured scope
entries.test_contract: Direct: usage at 99% of limit → allow or warn per threshold; at 100% → deny 'Internal budget exhausted'; negative: disabled/absent limit → allow; invalid: limitValue<=0 → deny with config reason
entries.rollback_or_disable: Set enabled=false on the limit row (evaluateBudget returns allow for disabled limits)

entries.name: api-key-cost-budget-schedules
entries.purpose: Per-API-key USD budgets with scheduled resets: setBudget configures daily/weekly/monthly limits + warning threshold + reset interval/time persisted in SQLite; checkBudget is enforced in the API-key policy chain where a budget-check failure fails CLOSED with 503 'Budget policy unavailable' and breaches deny the request; GET/POST /api/usage/budget (management-auth) exposes cost summaries and budget writes. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: high — spend control per key; the fail-closed 503 on budget-store error means a DB hiccup halts all budgeted keys' traffic (availability vs overspend tradeoff, deliberately closed)
entries.test_contract: Direct: set $0.01 daily budget, drive spend, assert denial past limit; fault: break the budget store and confirm 503 (not silent allow); reset: window rollover zeroes the period per schedule
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the key's budget config; checkBudget passes with no budget present

entries.name: budget-reset-registry-job
entries.purpose: JobRegistry interval job 'budget_reset' (default every 10min, floor 10s, OMNIROUTE_BUDGET_RESET_JOB_INTERVAL_MS) that syncs all budget schedules — processing due resets and recording run success/failure through the registry's safeRun rather than local try/catch. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — a stalled job leaves expired budgets un-reset (deny persists past window); interval floor prevents hot-loop misconfiguration
entries.test_contract: Direct: seed a budget whose reset is due, run the handler, assert recordsAffected==resetCount; scheduling: registry shows the interval registration and run records
entries.rollback_or_disable: Disable the job in the registry (enabled:false); schedules then reset lazily never — budgets stay at last state

entries.name: relay-token-rate-limit
entries.purpose: Relay-surface token rate limiting: checkRateLimit enforces per-relay-token minute and day windows (epoch-aligned buckets read from SQLite relay usage rows) before dispatching /api/v1/relay/chat/completions, returning allowed/remaining/resetIn for client headers. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: medium — the relay plane's only quota guard; DB-window math errors either over-admit relay traffic or lock out valid relay tokens
entries.test_contract: Direct: exceed the token's per-minute limit and assert rejection with resetIn; boundary: window rollover restores allowance; negative: unknown token id → allowed:false
entries.rollback_or_disable: Raise/remove the token's limits in relay_tokens; no global toggle

entries.name: registered-key-issuance-quota-check
entries.purpose: GET /api/v1/quotas/check?provider=&accountId= (authenticated) pre-validates whether a new registered key may be issued for a provider/account without issuing it — the dry-run front door to registered-key quota enforcement. [FACT]
entries.risk_class: low — read-only pre-check; the authoritative enforcement lives in the registered-keys issuance path itself
entries.test_contract: Direct: query a provider/account at its issuance cap → allowed:false with errorCode; negative: unauthenticated → 401
entries.rollback_or_disable: No runtime state; remove the route to drop the dry-run surface (issuance enforcement remains)

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED-prometheus-openmetrics-exporter
entries.purpose: Searched for a Prometheus/OpenMetrics /metrics exporter: case-insensitive grep for 'prometheus|openmetrics' across src/, open-sse/, packages/, package.json returned zero matches; the only metrics-export-shaped surface found is the OTLP GenAI routing-event sink (CAP-P6-016), which is traces, not scrape metrics. [FACT — absence, grep-verified]
entries.risk_class: low — absence of a scrape endpoint is an integration gap, not a defect; dashboards are HTML + JSON APIs instead

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED-distributed-session-store
entries.purpose: Searched for a distributed/persistent session store: sessionManager state is a process-local Map with a local setInterval sweeper; no Redis/external session backend exists for sticky sessions (contrast: the quota store HAS an optional Redis driver, CAP-P6-042 — sessions do not). [FACT — absence in modules read; INFERENCE that no other session store exists, corroborated by Coder-X review]
entries.risk_class: low — multi-replica deployments lose stickiness coherence and split the 200-session cap per replica
entries.test_contract: Grep sessionManager + redisQuotaStore contrast at any later snapshot

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED-per-ip-traffic-plane-rate-limit
entries.purpose: Searched for per-client-IP rate limiting on the /v1 traffic plane: the only client-plane request limiter keys on apiKeyInfo.id (rl:api_key:<id> window keys), so anonymous keyless traffic (REQUIRE_API_KEY=false default, P4) has no per-IP request-rate control on the inference path; the per-IP login throttle found by P4 (loginGuard) is management-plane only. [FACT — absence in policy chain; key-space is api_key by construction]
entries.risk_class: medium — on a keyless deployment the inference plane has no request-rate brake short of the structural admission gate (CAP-P6-036)
entries.test_contract: Re-check apiKeyPolicy + rateLimiter key space at any later snapshot
entries.rollback_or_disable: n/a

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED-external-log-shipping-sink
entries.purpose: Searched for external log shipping (syslog/fluentd/loki/HTTP drains): logging destinations are stdout, the local app.log file (DATA_DIR-anchored), and SQLite tables; no shipper configuration or drain endpoint exists in the modules read. [FACT — absence; corroborated by Coder-X review of the logging bundle]
entries.risk_class: low — log aggregation must scrape files/stdout externally (acceptable on the single-host LAN posture)
entries.test_contract: Grep logEnv/logRotation/proxyLogger destinations at any later snapshot

entries.name: NOT-ESTABLISHED-opentelemetry-sdk-request-tracing
entries.purpose: Searched for OpenTelemetry SDK-based request tracing (@opentelemetry/* packages): package.json carries no such dependency and the only OTel-shaped code is the deliberately SDK-free OTLP/HTTP routing-event sink (CAP-P6-016); the request pipeline itself is not span-instrumented. [FACT — absence; dependency-free design stated in the module doc]
entries.risk_class: low — end-to-end distributed tracing of requests is unavailable; only routing events can be exported

entries.purpose: Searched for a configuration to make quota-share enforcement fail-CLOSED: the engine documents fail-open as a fixed design decision (B16 — 'any error from store/plan/saturation is caught and treated as allow'), and grep for QUOTA_FAIL*/failClosed/fail_closed across src/lib/quota and quotaMonitor returned no toggle. [FACT — absence, grep-verified]
